Visit note | 2025-12-20 10:30 AM | Dr. Kamrul Hasan, Pulmonology | Patient: Tasnim Miah, 60, female. Mrs. Miah returns for review, reporting a tight chest whenever she is near dust or cold air, along with coughing at night and audible wheezing. She works as a shopkeeper and mentions her symptoms have been worse since construction dust started near her home in Motijheel. She denies fever or chest pain. On examination: SpO2 96%, BP 122/73 mmHg, pulse 82 bpm, weight 51 kg. Chest examination reveals scattered wheezes with good air entry bilaterally. Assessment: Bronchial asthma. Plan: chronic follow-up; continue current medicines, no new prescription issued today. She was advised to avoid dust and smoke, keep her bedroom well aired, and ensure correct inhaler technique. Follow-up in 1 month to check inhaler technique.
